findings.excerpt: [F4] Every compiled gate word is unitary because its letters lie in $G\subset SU(2)$ ([[def-qc-inverse-closed-dense-su2-gate-set]]). From the operator-norm definition ([[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]]), left multiplication by a unitary preserves norm because it preserves vector norms, and right multiplication preserves norm because it maps the unit sphere bijectively to itself.

missing_diagrams.diagram_kind: Wire-by-round graph encoding of a J/CZ circuit schedule
missing_diagrams.rationale: The definition maps each source wire and transport round to graph vertices and maps each schedule matching to inter-wire edges. An explicit small-instance graph would make the vertex order, input/output boundaries, and round-to-round measurement sweep easier to track.
missing_diagrams.draw_or_check: Draw rows for source wires j and columns s=0,…,R, with v_{j,s} at each position. Show horizontal edges v_{j,s−1}—v_{j,s}; for each matching pair {j,k} in M_s show a vertical CZ edge between v_{j,s−1} and v_{k,s−1}. Mark I at column 0 and O at column R; number the round-major, wire-minor measurement order over columns 0,…,R−1. Keep adaptive angles and Pauli-frame recurrences in the text or annotate one round with z^{s,*}=z^{s−1}⊕A_s x^{s−1}, x^s=b^s⊕z^{s,*}, z^s=x^{s−1}. No correctness claim should depend on the diagram.
missing_diagrams.status: candidate only; vertex/edge sets, boundary maps, ordering, and frame recurrences are stated in the source.

missing_diagrams.diagram_kind: Four-vertex open-graph pattern implementing CZ by two one-bit teleportations
missing_diagrams.rationale: The item has an explicit four-vertex graph with two measured inputs, two output vertices, a CZ edge between the inputs, four branch operators, and outcome-dependent corrections. A pattern/circuit sketch would make the wire roles and correction placement immediate.
missing_diagrams.draw_or_check: Use vertices 1,2 as inputs and 3,4 as outputs; draw edges {1,2}, {1,3}, {2,4}. Mark 1,2 measured in the H basis with outcomes b1,b2; mark output branch K_{b1b2}=1/2 (X^{b1}H⊗X^{b2}H)CZ and correction HX^{b1}⊗HX^{b2}, yielding 1/2 CZ|ψ⟩. Show all four branches have probability 1/4. Keep the mathematical proof independent of the picture.
missing_diagrams.status: candidate only; the graph, input/output assignment, branch map, and correction are fully specified in the source.

missing_diagrams.diagram_kind: Periodic square torus with primal/dual fundamental cycles and winding cuts
missing_diagrams.rationale: The statement identifies the quotient of cycles by face boundaries with two winding parities, using horizontal and vertical loops as basis representatives. A torus sketch would clarify the primal/dual correspondence and how cuts detect the two mod-2 coordinates.
missing_diagrams.draw_or_check: Draw a periodic square cellulation with a horizontal primal loop γ_h and vertical primal loop γ_v; add one vertical and one horizontal cut and label winding pairs (1,0) and (0,1). Add dual edges/faces in a distinct style and indicate the analogous dual loops and dual cuts. Annotate that face boundaries have zero winding and are quotiented out. The rank and quotient proof remains algebraic and independent of the drawing.
missing_diagrams.status: candidate only; cellulation, loops, cuts, winding parity values, and dual counterpart are stated in the source.
